as_told.title: Havana syndrome attributed to Russian microwave weaponry

plain: Havana syndrome, the unexplained illness reported by US diplomats and spies, is said to have been caused by Russian attacks going back to the 1980s, according to a report by 60 Minutes, the American TV news program. Michels says the piece came out recently, made together with the German magazine Der Spiegel. Eric Haseltine, a former senior official at the NSA, the US electronic spying agency, recalls the program raising the stakes: "if it's the Russians doing it to us, that's an act of war." On another episode Michels says the CIA and the NSA blame Russia and microwave weapons, and places it in the last couple of years, without mentioning the 1980s or the program. It is told because if true it would mean a foreign power has been quietly attacking American officials for decades.
